name: Simonds Ryder
role: Hiram preacher who joined briefly, then opposed the Church
dateNote: He was ordained an elder on 6 June 1831 and had left the Church by September 1831.
importance: Section 52 transfers to him the office taken from Heman Basset because of transgression. Ryder left within months and returned to leading the Disciples congregation at Hiram. Later accounts say a misspelling of his name in his commission troubled him, along with fears about consecration. Joseph Smith’s history names him among the mob that tarred and feathered Joseph at Hiram in March 1832.
connections: He had been a Disciples (Campbellite) leader at Hiram before joining. His case is tied to Heman Basset and to the Johnson family of Hiram.

sources.title: Symonds Ryder, Doctrine and Covenants Central

reviewNote: Birth (20 November 1792, Hartford, Vermont), death (1 August 1870, Hiram), ordination, and departure checked on JSP. Misspelling story and mob role are from Doctrine and Covenants Central and are reported as later accounts and Joseph Smith’s claim. Spelling varies (Symonds/Simonds, Rider/Ryder).
